`python3 budget.py 2026-09` now counts only September's transactions, and with no month it prints the same report as before. I ran it against your data: September leaves groceries 371.55, fuel 124.75, eating out 84.25 and household 101.60, and the no-month totals are unchanged.

One thing I added that you didn't ask for: every run prints a line to stderr saying how many transactions were counted, e.g. `2026-09: 6 of 12 transactions`. Without it, a mistyped or empty month such as `2025-01` shows every envelope at its full allocation with no hint why. Stdout is still just the report, so piping it is unaffected; say so if you'd rather drop the line.

A month that isn't `YYYY-MM` (like `sept` or `2026-13`) exits with code 2 and a usage message instead of producing a report.
